promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Skip Wednesday's tempo and get the right knee looked at by a physio or sports doctor before you run hard again. Next week is rest, a walk and a cautious test run only if the knee is pain-free.

flags.title: Long run cut short
flags.detail: planned 13 mi, you stopped at 8.5 mi with sharp pain from mile 7 and walked the last half mile. Your other four runs went as planned, including the tempo at 8:00/mi.

flags.title: Knee trend
flags.detail: pain went 2/10 Thu, 1/10 Sat, then a sharp 4/10 Sun, and it now aches on stairs. It is getting worse and showing up off the run, so watch walking and stairs as well as running.

flags.title: Return rule
flags.detail: run only when walking and stairs are 0/10. Stop and walk home at the first knee pain; one bad test run means rest, not a retry the next day.

flags.title: Long-run effort
flags.detail: your last three long runs averaged 146 to 147 bpm with up to 60% in zone 3. Once you are back, hold long runs under 145 so they stay easy.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
**Is this an IT band thing?** I can't tell you that, and a guess from a distance could send you down the wrong path. Pain on the outside of the knee that is sharper on downhills has several possible causes. A physio or sports medicine doctor can tell them apart by examining you. What I can see is that the pain grew over three runs, forced you to stop and now shows up on stairs. That is enough reason to get it checked this week.

**Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?** No, drop it. Running at 8:00/mi puts more load through the knee than easy running, and the knee got worse across last week. A hard session is the first thing to come back, after you have run easy and pain-free for a while. Don't make the session up later.

new.analysis:
## What happened

The week followed the plan until Sunday. Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday were run as planned, and the tempo hit its 8:00/mi target with no fade. The long run is where it changed: you planned 13 mi and finished 9 mi, including a half mile of walking, because of the knee.

The knee is the story of the week, and the order of events matters. It was tight on the last hill Thursday, tight before the run Saturday, and sharp from mile 7 on Sunday. Today it hurts on stairs. A problem that is growing and no longer limited to running is one to get examined, not one to train through.

## Why the plan is cut back so far

Running through a knee that is getting worse is how a one-week problem becomes a six-week problem. You are 10 weeks from the race, so there is room to lose a week or two and still build properly. A lighter week was also coming after several weeks of building, so the loss of volume costs you less than it looks.

I would rather you arrive at the start line healthy at 90% of the planned mileage than chase every mile now. The test runs in the plan are gated on pain scores, not on the calendar. If the professional tells you to hold off running, follow them over anything I have written.

## How the build restarts

When the knee is pain-free for daily life and easy running, volume comes back first, then the long run, then the quality work. The tempo and marathon-pace segments come last. The 3:45 goal is not off the table, but I will reassess it after I know what the professional found and how the test runs go.

The easy-running share of 76% looks low against the 80% target. A week with a threshold session pushes it down through the warm-up, cool-down and recoveries, so it is not a concern. The more useful point is the long-run effort. Heart rate near 147 at 10:00/mi is working harder than easy running at 139, and that effort adds up over a long build.

## What I need next time

In your next check-in, tell me what the professional said, your pain score on stairs each morning, and how each test run felt. If you skip a run because of the knee, note it. That is useful information, not a failure.

safetyCallouts.title: Get the right knee assessed this week.
safetyCallouts.body: The pain rose from 2/10 to a sharp 4/10 over three runs, made you stop, and now aches on stairs. See a physio or sports medicine doctor before you do any hard running. Get seen promptly if it swells, locks, gives way, or hurts at rest or at night.
